title: Cohort-traceback fanout conductor with interruptible rollback and explainable recovery
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Add a Cohort Traceback Fanout Conductor that enables session-coherent A/B promotions, interruptible rollbacks, and a lightweight explainable rollback oracle. Includes new telemetry hooks and a dry-run smoke-replay mode for pre-promote validation.
description:
Summary: Introduces the 'Cohort Traceback Fanout Conductor' (CTFC), a rollout controller that prioritizes session-coherent cohorts for canary/A-B promotions, supports interruptible rollbacks mid-fanout, and exposes an explainable rollback oracle that surfaces the minimal contributing signals when a promote fails.

Motivation: Recent incidents showed large blast radii when promotions ignored session affinity and when rollbacks were binary and opaque. CTFC reduces user-visible regressions by ensuring fans are constrained to cohort boundaries, enabling on-the-fly interruption, and providing triageable telemetry to SREs and PMs.

Changes:
- New controller binary: controllers/ctfc with core reconcile loop, progress checkpointing, and interrupt logic.
- Exhaustive telemetry: telemetry/ctfc_metrics.go + new events for "fanout_step", "rollback_interrupt", and "counterfactual_smoke".
- Explainable rollback oracle: a modular evaluator that runs a compact counterfactual smoke replay on recent samples and returns ranked signal contributions.
- Safety budget integration: honor existing rollout budget tokens and expose a credit refund when early-interrupts avoid downstream degradation.
- Dry-run mode: a CLI flag and API path that runs validation without committing traffic.
- Tests: e2e smoke harness that replays recorded traffic and unit tests for oracle scorer.

Review thread (abridged):
- Daniel Kim (reviewer): "Nice separation of concerns between fanout and oracle. Two asks: (1) ensure the oracle's counterfactual runner limits sample size by default to avoid CPU spikes; (2) add a feature flag gating dry-run in production clusters."
- Priya (author): "Addressed both: default sample cap is 200 and feature flag 'ctfc.dryrun.enabled' added; updated tests to assert cap and gating."
- Maya Chen: "Can we preserve KV-cache warmup for session-affine buckets? Without it some sessions see latency spikes when promoted."
- Priya: "Added a warmup step that performs lightweight KV priming for the first N sessions in a cohort; configurable via rollout config."
- Omar Ruiz: "Telemetry looks good; can you emit an event for 'fanout_resume' as well? It's helpful when resuming after interruption."
- Priya: "Added fanout_resume event and templatized the alert rule in observability package."

CI summary:
- unit: pass

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the public API additive and optional; default rollout controllers remain unchanged unless organizations opt into CTFC via rollout policy. The explainable oracle is designed for triage not for automated overrides; the team can later expose a trust score if product requires it. Related: Linear ENG-4821, SUP-3101 (customer-reported session-affinity regression), design notes at /design/ctfc.md
notes: Author verified in staging with canary on two customer clusters. Performance impact observed: median reconcile loop CPU +7% under active promotions; telemetry budget token accounting mitigates sustained load. Ops runbook attached to observability/playbooks/ctfc-runbook.md
